note: The pinned build toolchain of BUILD MASHUP (same pins as build/EXPECTED.json and docs/BUILDING.md; archive names, URLs and sha256 identical to tools/prepare_deps.py). A download happens only after you confirm it for that one tool; the licence notice below is shown first. Nothing is installed system-wide: archives are verified (sha256) and unpacked into the tools folder you choose. No administrator rights, no PATH or registry change.

tools.licence: Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception (LLVM, Clang, LLD) + the mingw-w64 licences (headers and runtime; ZPL-2.1 and others)

The compiler runtime pieces linked into programs it builds are under those licences. Read the licence files in the archive.

tools.name: Vulkan-Headers + import library
tools.licence_note: The Khronos Vulkan headers are available under the Apache License 2.0 or the MIT licence (LICENSE.md in the archive). The import library libvulkan-1.dll.a is generated on this PC (llvm-mingw's gendef + llvm-dlltool) from the export list of your driver's System32\vulkan-1.dll; the host does not import it.

tools.name: glslang (built here, static)
tools.licence: BSD-3-Clause, BSD-2-Clause, MIT, Apache-2.0 and other licences per file (LICENSE.txt in the archive)
tools.licence_note: glslang is source code under several permissive licences listed in its LICENSE.txt; it is compiled here as static libraries with llvm-mingw, CMake and Ninja (a few minutes).

tools.name: Git for Windows (PortableGit)
tools.licence: GPL-2.0-only (Git) + the licences of the bundled components
tools.licence_note: Git is distributed under the GNU General Public License version 2; PortableGit bundles other programs under their own licences (listed in the unpacked folder). The download is a 7-Zip self-extractor: it is started once (after the sha256 check) to unpack into the tools folder and shows a small progress window. Only used to read the pinned upstream sources (git archive / git clone).

tools.name: Python environment with capstone 5.0.9 (for the upstream recompiler)
tools.licence_note: capstone (the disassembly framework and its Python binding) is distributed under the BSD 3-Clause licence. A private Python environment is made in the tools folder with this launcher's Python (python -m venv) and pip installs capstone==5.0.9 from the Python Package Index; the installed files are then checked against the sha256 values below (from the reference build).
